mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) below 1.2 million units signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 5% for three consecutive months is associated with reduced consumer confidence and spending, which depresses earnings across sectors and leads to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for two consecutive months signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate revenue and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the unemployment rate and a fall in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 100,000 in a month indicate accelerating labor market weakness, which reduces consumer demand and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises AND PAYEMS falls by > 100,000 in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above the previous year's level by more than 5% for three consecutive months signals a shift from spending to saving, which reduces aggregate demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > previous year by > 5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both the federal funds rate and CPI inflation below 2% for two consecutive months signals an easing policy stance with stable prices, which supports risk asset valuations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS falls AND CPIAUCSL < 2.0 for 2 consecutive months
regime_hint: loose monetary policy with low inflation
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.4% for four consecutive months signals an expansion in manufacturing activity, which boosts earnings expectations and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change > 0.4% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
